roles.summary: Leads the elected state government and heads the Council of Ministers.
tasks: Sets the government’s overall policy direction and priorities
Coordinates the work of ministers and the departments held by the CM
Heads the Council of Ministers that aids and advises the Governor
roles.description: Heads the Council of Ministers and gives political direction to the elected state government. Departmental decisions are processed through the state’s business rules and the competent minister, Cabinet or authorised official.
actions: Set government priorities and coordinate ministerial policy
Lead Cabinet consideration of matters requiring a collective decision
Review the portfolios held by the CM and communicate constitutionally required information to the Governor
limits: The CM does not exercise the judicial powers of courts or the independent statutory powers of every commission.
roles.example: A proposal involving several departments can be coordinated and placed through the required government decision process.

Agree collective policy and legislative proposals
Coordinate decisions requiring more than one portfolio
limits: A Cabinet decision still needs the applicable legal authority, appropriation and implementation orders.
roles.example: A major cross-department proposal can be considered collectively before the responsible departments implement the authorised decision.

roles.summary: The state’s senior administrative officer, coordinating government administration.
tasks: Coordinates work across departments and administrative priorities

Heads the General Administration Department

actions: Convene interdepartmental reviews and resolve administrative coordination issues
Review implementation and escalate matters requiring government decisions
Process the administrative matters allocated to the office
limits: The office cannot replace a court or bypass a power reserved to a minister, statutory body or other competent authority.
